The Studio

Learning from 3.8 billion years of research and development

The Nature's Intelligence Studio is a TIDE Centre initiative, developed in partnership with CAF, that accelerates nature-inspired innovation for sustainable development. It translates principles observed in biological systems, especially in biodiversity-rich regions such as the Amazon, into practical and scalable technologies for the energy transition, while ensuring fair benefit-sharing with the communities whose biodiversity makes discovery possible.

Launched at
COP30

Belém, Brazil · November 2025
Launched by Oxford's TIDE Centre at the UN Climate Change Conference in the Amazon.

Three pillars
01

Knowledge production and advocacy

Generating evidence on nature-inspired solutions and making the case for them among policymakers, industry and the public.

02

Supply and demand of nature-inspired innovation

Building a pipeline of bio-inspired ventures (supply), understanding the needs of industry (demand), and connecting the two.

03

Benefit-sharing

Ensuring that innovation inspired by biodiversity creates value for the communities and countries where that biodiversity is found.

What we do
With CAF

Nature's Intelligence Ideathon

Latin America's first ideathon dedicated to biomimicry, connecting researchers and entrepreneurs with mentors, investors and partners.

With Asteria

Energy Atlas of Nature's Solutions

An AI-powered platform connecting industrial energy challenges to biological models drawn from over 4 million scientific articles. Explore the Atlas

TIDE Working Papers

Research

Research on biomimicry, AI and energy, such as Working Paper 90: AI, Biodiversity & Energy.

Fair and equitable

Benefit-Sharing Framework

A legal framework so that the communities whose biodiversity underpins discovery share in the value it creates.

Nature's Intelligence Ideathon 2026

Latin America's first ideathon dedicated to biomimicry

An open call from January to April 2026 invited teams across the region to answer ten sustainability challenges with solutions inspired by nature. The ten finalist teams met in Rio de Janeiro on 3 and 4 August 2026, at the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden and Casa FIRJAN.
